name: SN Manta Submersible Glider
description: A one-person submersible that moves through water like a mechanical ray — flat, silent, and nearly undetectable. The Manta uses buoyancy changes and wing surfaces to glide through the Great Lakes with minimal power consumption, surfacing only when necessary. Originally designed for naval reconnaissance, civilian versions have found their way to smugglers, researchers, and anyone who needs to move beneath the lake surface without being seen. The ride is claustrophobic, cold, and absolutely silent — just you and the dark water and whatever is swimming alongside you.
propulsion: Buoyancy-driven glide, electric thrust for maneuvering
range: 200 km on a single battery charge
autonomy: Pilot-operated, AI depth and trim management
armament: None standard. Torpedo tube on military variants (rumored).
common_usage: Underwater reconnaissance, smuggling, research, crossing the lake unseen.
story_hooks: A Manta pilot on a routine smuggling run encounters another Manta — one that isn't in any registry and doesn't respond to hails
The Manta's sonar picks up something pacing it in the deep water, matching speed and depth changes perfectly
related_entities: Dredge Mining Collective Underwater Resource Extraction Platform
physical_description: A sleek, flattened hull of brushed titanium and composite polymer, roughly three meters long with swept-back wing surfaces that fold against its body. The Manta's exterior bears the salt-stained patina of frequent submersion—corroded access panels, patched welds, and a single reinforced viewport of scratched polymer that reveals nothing of the cramped interior. Navigation lights sit dormant along its dorsal ridge, dark as dead eyes.
visual_prompt: Sterling-Nakamura Manta submersible, one-person underwater vessel, sleek ray-like form, brushed titanium hull with composite panels, salt-corroded weathering, folded wing surfaces, reinforced viewport, gritty neo-noir aesthetic, detailed product photography, dark water-stained background, industrial decay, cyberpunk near-future, moody lighting, worn military-grade engineering
